peer_results.rationale: While AMD discusses IP protection (amd_2024_1_D075) and time-to-market in the context of embedded market shifts (amd_2024_1_D037), it does not link IP protection to manufacturing outsourcing decisions nor does it discuss a strategic rationale for outsourcing manufacturing operations in the provided candidates. The AMD disclosures focus on legal portfolio size and market architecture trends rather than the manufacturing supply chain strategy central to AVGO's topic.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel manufactures a majority of its products in its own facilities using proprietary technologies to optimize performance, shorten time-to-market, and scale high-volume products.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and INTC explicitly cite 'shortening/accelerating time-to-market' as a primary strategic benefit of their respective manufacturing models, but they achieve this through opposite operational structures. AVGO attributes these benefits to its outsourcing model, stating it uses outsourcing to 'protect our IP and accelerate time to market for our products' (avgo_2024_1_P035_S005). In contrast, INTC claims that its internal manufacturing using proprietary technologies allows it to 'shorten time-to-market for new product introductions, and more quickly scale products in high volume' (intc_2024_1_P011_S002).

sentences.text: By doing so, we can protect our IP and accelerate time to market for our products.
This enables us to optimize performance, shorten time-to-market for new product introductions, and more quickly scale products in high volume.

peer_results.rationale: MU's disclosure (mu_2024_1_D053) mentions outsourcing assembly services but focuses on product forms and proprietary testing technology rather than a strategic rationale for outsourcing tied to IP protection or time-to-market acceleration in the same manner as AVGO. The IP disclosure (mu_2024_1_D066) focuses on monetization via licensing, which is a distinct business model from AVGO's manufacturing-centric IP protection strategy.

NVDA's disclosures (nvda_2024_1_D035, nvda_2024_1_D044) focus on IP licensing strategies and legal protection risks, particularly regarding foreign jurisdictions. It does not discuss manufacturing outsourcing as a vehicle for IP protection or time-to-market acceleration, nor does it describe its manufacturing operations in the context of strategic rationale comparable to AVGO.

QCOM's disclosures (qcom_2024_1_D041, qcom_2024_1_D042) detail its QTL licensing model and revenue mechanics for wireless patents. It does not discuss manufacturing outsourcing, IP protection via manufacturing partners, or time-to-market strategies related to its supply chain operations in the provided candidates.
